title: Runtime env overrides: BUN_OPTIONS and BUN_BE_BUN reach the packaged executable
description: Found while delivering WCLI-16 (measured on bun 1.3.14, macOS arm64). The executable built with --no-compile-autoload-dotenv/bunfig ignores the working directory's bunfig.toml and .env, but two inherited environment variables are still honoured by the embedded runtime before any Ward code runs: (1) BUN_OPTIONS="--preload ./x.ts" preloads arbitrary code into the ward process; (2) BUN_BE_BUN=1 turns the executable into the full bun CLI, which runs arbitrary scripts (-e) under Ward's executable identity and loads the working directory's bunfig.toml again. A check inside Ward cannot close (1), because the preload runs first and can remove the variable. No bun build flag disables either. Spec §4.2 already disclaims arbitrary code with equivalent authority, so the open question is not severity but binding: if WCLI-3 binds the vault key's keychain ACL to the ward executable's code identity, (2) makes that binding hollow, since any code can run as that executable. Needs a decision under WCLI-3 (opum-doc) before code: accept and document, launch through a small native launcher that scrubs the environment, or choose a runtime without these switches.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A decision recorded in opum-doc states whether the packaged executable must resist BUN_OPTIONS and BUN_BE_BUN, with the measurement it rests on
If it must: a test runs the packaged executable with BUN_OPTIONS preloading a marker-writing file and with BUN_BE_BUN=1 -e, and neither runs code; the same test against the WCLI-16 executable fails
If it need not: SECURITY.md or the threat-model doc names both variables as a stated limitation

implementationNotes: Sibling found in the WCLI-5 review, 2026-09-28: @napi-rs/keyring loads any module named by NAPI_RS_NATIVE_LIBRARY_PATH in place of its native binding. Measured: a compiled probe loaded a harmless planted module. Unlike BUN_OPTIONS and BUN_BE_BUN, the binding reads this variable only when it is first imported, after src/cli/guard.ts has run. The guard now deletes the variable, and a compiled test with an unguarded control shows the override loading only without the guard. It is closed, not merely accepted.

FINDING FROM WCLI-10 (2026-09-29): Bun 1.3.14's node:https honours HTTPS_PROXY / HTTP_PROXY from the environment, and no in-process option defeats it. This belongs here because it is the same family this task exists for - ambient runtime environment changing what the packaged Ward binary does without Ward asking.

MEASURED, not inferred. A net listener on 127.0.0.1, and an https request to a host whose custom `lookup` hook returns a public address. With HTTPS_PROXY pointed at the listener, the connection went to the LISTENER while the lookup hook still ran for the destination hostname. That second half is the dangerous one: an address-validating hook reported a binding that was not the one used, so a preflight check of the kind spec 9.3 describes would have been satisfied by a request that went somewhere else.

WHAT DOES NOT WORK - each tried and each failed to change the dial: option `proxy: ""`; option `proxy: false`; an explicit `new https.Agent({ keepAlive: false })`; `agent.createConnection` (never called at all - Bun short-circuits that path to its own fetch layer, so the socket is never the caller's); and `delete process.env.HTTPS_PROXY` in-process, because Bun reads the proxy variables when the process starts rather than per request. `NO_PROXY=*` set in-process DOES defeat it, and was rejected as the mechanism for Ward: it would make a security property depend on an environment variable whose failure mode is silent proxying.

WHAT WARD DOES INSTEAD, as the workaround spec-consistent with this task's own guidance: WCLI-10's transport dials with tls.connect, which is unaffected by the ambient proxy because it consults nothing but the address it is given, and resolves once, judges every address, then dials the validated literal with the hostname supplied separately as the SNI name. Verified positively: authorized=true, and Bun refuses an IP passed as servername outright (ERR_INVALID_ARG_VALUE). The positive control lives in test/fixtures/transport-proxy-probe.ts: in one process with HTTPS_PROXY set, node:https must reach the parent's listener and this transport must not, and the assertion is the pair.

WHAT THIS TASK SHOULD TAKE FROM IT. The proxy variables are one member of a class - ambient environment read by the runtime before Ward's own code runs - and BUN_OPTIONS and BUN_BE_BUN are two others already named in this task's title. The transferable lesson is the control shape rather than the finding: a claim that "the environment cannot affect X" is only evidence when the same invocation shows the variable being live somewhere it should be, because an inert variable and a defeated one produce identical clean output.

Reported to opum-agent 2026-09-29. Not filed against Bun; the fleet's policy is to hand the owning session a report, not to act on it.
